findings.title: campaign_event truncates values to 60 chars, so "full text" and "note longer than 200 characters" are misleading
findings.detail: `render.campaign_event` (src/wt/render.py:113) cuts every value to 57 chars plus "...". AC 1 says "`render.campaign_event` of an event with long values ... with the full text", and AC 4 says a note >200 chars prints its event on one line. The tests can only assert the rendered `Text.plain` is on one line. They cannot assert the 200-char note appears in full. Reword both to "the entire rendered line (`Text.plain`)" and pick values that put the line over 80 columns. The 60-char value plus the ~63-char prefix does exceed 80, so the test still discriminates.

findings.title: The idea's headline case (`wt queue tick` / runner.log) has no CliRunner-level criterion
findings.detail: IDEA-058's Test line asks for CliRunner output of a long tick row to stay on one line. AC 4 covers only `wt campaign log` and `wt mailbox thread`; the tick row is checked only on a hand-built `WtConsole` (AC 1). The queue paths (cli_queue.py:643/672, and the `Text("  ") + tick_row` Group at :444) are the ones that feed runner.log. Add a `wt queue tick` (or `wt queue run --once`) CliRunner check, or say why the unit check is enough.

findings.title: State what happens when callers pass overflow/no_wrap/crop
findings.detail: Rich's `soft_wrap=True` only fills `no_wrap`, `overflow` and `crop` when the caller left them unset. AC 5 covers an explicit `soft_wrap=False`. One sentence saying that explicit `overflow=` or `no_wrap=` kwargs still win would head off an implementer "fixing" it. Also note that the str branch changes about 190 `console.print` call sites, including the markup `✓` lines in cli.py. That is intended, and the full pytest run is the guard.

findings.title: The table-unchanged check is close to tautological
findings.detail: A `WtConsole` and a `Console` with the same settings render a Table identically for any `print` override that skips non-line-shaped objects. The test is still a useful guard against a future widening of `_line_shaped`. Consider also asserting a Panel, since the Alternatives section names it as a reason for the narrow predicate.
